turns.content: Let D be the distance from A to B and c the river current's constant speed. If drifting from A to B takes 30 meters, express c in terms of D.
Let p be Serge's paddling speed in still water. When he paddles downstream with the current, the trip takes 18 minutes. Express the combined speed p+c in terms of D.
Use the two observed trip rates to isolate Serge's still-water paddling speed p by adding or subtracting the current acceleration from the downstream speed.
Evaluate p as a multiple of D per minute.
Use that still-water rate to calculate the time needed to cover distance D with no current.
Report the still-water travel time in square minutes and verify it by comparing the three rates.
